newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed as summer lull sets in.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed as summer lull sets in.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mixed in sluggish business on Wednesday which traders described as the beginning of the summer slide. Drugs firm Pliva and brewery Karlovacka Pivovara dominated trade.
"Prices of most liquid stocks are stagnating, which may bring about a mild slide towards the end of July," Domagoj Grabovac of Fima brokerage said.
Fully-listed Pliva was the day's most active stock with 2,080 shares sold. It fell five kuna to 485, but traders said no major changes were on the cards.
Another blue chip Zagrebacka Banka added 57 kuna or 2.9 percent to 2,020 kuna on a modest volume of 314.
"Both heavyweights are recovering, but their present prices are realistic and we expect stagnation," Hrvoje Bujanovic of CAIB told Reuters.
He cited the bank's preferred 3E-series which has been on a steady rise for weeks as one of the market favourites. It gained ten kuna to 1,510 kuna on volume of 633 units.
Karlovacka Pivovara, subsidiary of Chile's Cervecerias brewery, was the second most sought-after stock accounting for 20 percent of trade. It sold 2,079 shares, closing flat at 560 kuna.
"This is a high quality share with a bright future ahead," Bujanovic said.
Of 13 issues three rose, five fell and five were flat.
Volume fell to 10,375 from 12,489 units and turnover to 5.0 million kuna from 7.3 on Tuesday.
Top gainer was electric cable maker Elka which added five kuna or 3.2 percent to 150 kuna on volume of 245 shares and traders said further growth was possible despite the summer approaching.

Hotelier Riviera led the decliners, losing four kuna or 2.6 percent to 146 with 328 shares sold, but the other three active hoteliers stood their ground. Jadranturist was the most active one selling 1,103 units at 265 kuna.
